technology.summary: Today's technology news includes the announcement of Microsoft's new AI chip, which will make the company less reliant on Nvidia's GPUs. The Fitbit Edge, a new fitness tracker, has also been unveiled. Amazon's use of over 1 million robot workers has raised questions about the future of human employees. TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 will focus on building enduring companies in the AI era. Other news includes a former Plaud exec raising $26 million for an AI app, the upcoming Apple "Welcome Home" event, and the rise and fall of the LeapPad.

finance.summary:
Today's most important finance news includes a landmark ruling by the Supreme Court of India, which has urged a probe into reports of hospitals directing patients to specific pharmacies for their medications, leading to a 5% drop in the BSE Hospitals Index.

In other news, the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India have teamed up to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market.

A resurgent El Niño pattern risks deepening a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, threatening to push yields higher.

Market experts have also shared their top stock picks for 1 October.

politics.summary:
The Delhi High Court has dismissed pleas for an SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence.

The Supreme Court is set to list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Congress has claimed that tribal students headed for a Mumbai protest were detained and threatened with police cases.

In other news, Donald Trump has cited a non-existent Indian election to call the US electoral process 'corrupt'.
